blocks: ## T01 - the run record says what ran, why, and where the time went (FR-002, FR-005)
## T02 - a tooling change no longer runs everything (FR-001)
## T03 - the landing waits only on what can refuse it (FR-003, FR-004)
## T05 - a landing runs what its change reaches (FR-006)

decisions.summary: runstats.py phase marks; done/test recipes mark each phase; end returns phases
decisions.why: Implements FR-005 / GM item 5.

decisions.summary: LOGRUN omits plan_mode/plan_reason/selected when the gate stopped before its test phase (no plan, nothing selected)
decisions.why: Physically nothing to record: no plan was made and no tests ran, so no full run occurred and GM item 2 ('every full run') is untouched.

decisions.summary: LOGRUN omits the reason (or reads a plan.json not written by this run) for a full test run that did not go through the planner - e.g. test-full or FR-006's background refresh
decisions.why: GM item 2 says the reason for EVERY full run; FR-002 is a MUST. Recording a reason is not impossible (the target knows it is test-full / the refresh). The block's 'left out where its source is absent' is not confined to the no-test-phase case, the plan itself adds a new full run (the refresh), and a stale plan.json from an earlier run would record a wrong reason - the mechanism cannot reach its stated purpose. Fix: every run of the test phase writes this run's plan.json (planner, or the target with its own reason such as test-full / refresh) before LOGRUN reads it, and LOGRUN reads only this run's plan; absence then means only that no tests ran.

decisions.summary: gate_config_hash over ci/, pipeline/, switches.py, _invocation.py, tests/conftest.py, tests/_scope.py, pinned lockfiles, pyproject pytest/coverage tables, Makefile test/test-full recipes and referenced variables minus help comments; plan full on gate_config move, not on tooling alone; missing key counts as moved once
decisions.why: Carries FR-001 and SC-001 (test target recipe, coverage table, requirements.txt full; help line, requirements*.in incremental). Premise not verifiable from the bundle: every non-lockfile path listed is already in today's TOOLING_PATHS; if one is not, D3 adds a full trigger outside FR-001's 'of the paths the tooling hash covers' and the block must be amended.

decisions.summary: scripts moved, gate_config not: select tests/tooling and tests/hooks modules plus every module (or transitively imported tests/ helper) whose source contains substring 'scripts'; reuse_tooling; gate_full becomes gate_reuses
decisions.why: FR-001's static loose rule, and the request's parenthetical that tooling tests are reused per test on their reads; the gate_reuses change is the mechanism that reuse requires on an incremental plan.

decisions.summary: cohort-landing runs fixed seeds and pinned rows beside the gate; fresh block started detached after a successful push, one at a time under a lock; cohort_gate.check needs no fresh block on a landing record
decisions.why: FR-003 / GM item 3. 'One at a time' read as serializing (a later fresh block waits); a lock that dropped a landing's fresh block would narrow FR-003's MUST and is not ruled here.

decisions.summary: cover_changed.py runs beside make done; non-zero stops the gate's group and refuses with its lines; cheap_refusals no longer runs it
decisions.why: FR-004 / GM item 4.

decisions.summary: scripts/measure/gate_costs.py fits fixed + per-test cost from run records; 'incremental drift' compares a full baseline with the merged one
decisions.why: FR-007 / GM item 6; the drift count serves FR-006's refresh rule, which the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The gate outside a landing keeps FULL_FRACTION; landings pass INCR_NO_CUTOFF=1
decisions.why: GM item 6: 'Drop the 60% cutoff from landings'.

decisions.summary: Cutoff/refresh rule deferred to T04's numbers, amended into the spec and reviewed
decisions.why: FR-007 requires the rule to wait on the measurement; decides nothing yet. When re-answered, the refresh's run record must carry its full-run reason (see D2b).

decisions.summary: SC-006's measured landing may be T05's own landing
decisions.why: T05 edits l7r/diagram/ci/, which D3 puts in gate_config, so its landing plans full by its own change and cannot exhibit FR-001 or FR-006 - the very thing measured against T26's 8.8 minutes. 'The next real landing' is word-plausible; SC-006's class ('an engine landing after a tooling change') and the purpose defeat it. Fix: the measured landing is the first whose own change does not move gate_config, whose baseline already carries the gate_config key, and which has a scripts/ change since its baseline - confirmed by plan_mode incremental in its T01 record.

decisions.summary: SC-006's measured landing may be feature 405's next task
decisions.why: An engine landing after a tooling change, as SC-006 asks - provided it meets D9a's criterion (does not move gate_config, baseline carries the key, scripts/ changed since baseline).

blocks: ## T01 - the run record says what ran, why, and where the time went (FR-002, FR-005)
## T02 - a tooling change no longer runs everything (FR-001)
## T03 - the landing waits only on what can refuse it (FR-003, FR-004)
## T05 - a landing runs what its change reaches (FR-006)

decisions.summary: runstats.py phase marks; done and test recipes mark each phase; end returns phases {name: seconds}
decisions.why: Request item 5 and FR-005 (each phase's seconds in the run record).

decisions.summary: every test-phase run writes its own plan (planner's, or its own with a reason for make test-full, INCREMENTAL=0, FULL=1, the background refresh); LOGRUN reads only this run's result and adds plan_mode, plan_reason, selected, collected
decisions.why: Request item 2 ('the reason for every full run') and FR-002; covering runs that bypass the planner is what 'every full run' requires, not extra scope.

decisions.summary: gate_config_hash over l7r/diagram/ci, pipeline, switches.py, _invocation.py, tests/conftest.py, tests/_scope.py, the pinned lockfiles, pyproject [tool.pytest*]/[tool.coverage*], and the Makefile test/test-full recipes with their variables closed over and ## help comments stripped; plan goes full on gate_config, no longer on the tooling hash alone
decisions.why: Request item 1 narrows exactly scripts/, the Makefile outside the lines that shape the test run, pyproject outside its pytest and coverage sections, and keeps lockfiles; D3 does each (help line incremental, test recipe full, lockfile full, as SC-001 states). The other paths it keeps as full triggers are today's TOOLING_PATHS, which the request did not ask to narrow. US1 scenario 3, which FR-001 cites for 'the gate's own machinery', was not in the bundle; judged on FR-001's words and the request's four classes.

decisions.summary: a second hash for the planner rather than removing scripts/ from tooling_hash, which keeps deciding when tooling tests rerun
decisions.why: Mechanism choice; FR-001 requires the tooling tests be reused on their recorded reads, which this keeps.

decisions.summary: on a scripts/-only move, select tests/tooling/ and tests/hooks/ modules and every other module whose source or transitively imported tests/ helper contains the substring 'scripts'; reuse_tooling flag deselects tooling tests with unchanged reads, and incremental carry copies their baseline coverage
decisions.why: FR-001 verbatim, including the loose reading and the transitive helper (SC-001's two named cases); the carry keeps reused tests' coverage, so nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: cohort-landing runs the fixed seeds and pinned rows (N=48 FRESH=0) beside the gate; the fresh block runs detached after a successful push, one at a time behind a lock that waits rather than skips; cohort_gate accepts a landing record without a fresh block
decisions.why: Request item 3 and FR-003 (fresh block after the push and off the path; fixed seeds and pinned rows stay beside the gate with their refusal).

decisions.summary: cover_changed.py runs beside make done; on non-zero exit the gate's group is stopped and the landing refused with its lines; removed from cheap_refusals
decisions.why: Request item 4 and FR-004.

decisions.summary: scripts/measure/gate_costs.py reads dev/run-log/: table of runs, least-squares fit of test-phase seconds on selected count, and the selection's growth against landings since the last full run
decisions.why: Request item 6 and FR-007 (fixed and per-test cost from real landings). The growth figure is what the refresh rule FR-006 must rest on; extra measurement in service of the request, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: growth since the last full run replaces 'drift of a merged baseline' (the baseline is the last full run, never merged); at least three planned-incremental and two full samples, incremental ones from later landings
decisions.why: Corrects the premise the earlier block measured against; still measures the fixed and per-test cost on a few real landings as item 6 asks.

decisions.summary: the landing's gate passes INCR_NO_CUTOFF=1; the gate outside a landing keeps FULL_FRACTION
decisions.why: Request item 6 says 'drop the 60% cutoff from landings'; SC-004 tests it at a landing. Keeping the fraction elsewhere is the request's own scope.

decisions.summary: the refresh rule deferred to T04's numbers, amended into FR-006 and reviewed then; the refresh run's record carries 'refresh: <trigger>'
decisions.why: Item 6 and FR-006/FR-007 require the rule to rest on the measured costs; deferral until they exist is what was asked. The amendment will be reviewed on its own.

decisions.summary: T06 measures the first landing whose own change does not move gate_config, whose baseline carries the gate_config key, and which has a scripts/ change since its baseline, confirmed by plan_mode: incremental
decisions.why: Item 1 says 'the gate measured on the next real landing'; D9 picks the first qualifying one rather than the literal next. Each condition judged separately: 'a scripts/ change since its baseline' is SC-006's 'after a tooling change' (accepted spec). 'Own change does not move gate_config' follows from item 1's own words that test-configuration and lockfile changes 'still do' force full; a landing the GM's rule sends to full cannot show item 1's saving, so measuring it would defeat the measurement's purpose. 'Baseline carries the key' has no anchor in the request or spec; it is an artifact of D3's migration ('a baseline without the key counts as moved, once'), costs at most the one landing after T02, and the plan_mode check keeps it honest. D9 does not say 'engine', which SC-006 requires; the T06 Approach constraint ('a real engine landing after a tooling change') supplies it, so not blocking.

decisions.summary: The 60% cutoff (FULL_FRACTION) is dropped for landings only (make land passes INCR_NO_CUTOFF=1); a gate run outside a landing keeps it.
decisions.why: Item 6 says 'Drop the 60% cutoff from landings', and the spec's US1 scenario 4 names landings. Keeping the cutoff for a gate run outside a landing is the literal scope of the request, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.summary: Refresh after a push only where the landing's gate ran incremental and selected at least REFRESH_FRACTION (0.25) of its baseline. Refreshing after every incremental landing is rejected.
decisions.why: FR-006 (amended) settles the 25% rule, and the GM's amendment 1 says 'land T05 now with the 25% rule'. The rejected exit is not something the spec required.

decisions.summary: The refresh runs in a detached worktree at the pushed commit, under a lock, started detached by land.py, never in the clone itself.
decisions.why: FR-006 requires a full run in a detached worktree at the pushed commit, under a lock, after the push and never on a landing's path. Item 6's 'refresh the baseline in the background' is carried by this.

decisions.summary: The refresh runs `make done INCR_FORCE="refresh: <n> of <N> baseline tests selected"` in the worktree.
decisions.why: FR-006 gives the reason string verbatim. Forcing full mode through INCR_FORCE is how the spec's 'full gate run' is carried out, and the earlier CLEAR D8 already fixed that the refresh record carries its reason (D2/FR-002).

decisions.summary: On green, the worktree's gate-baseline/ is copied into the clone's with each coverage path rewritten to the clone's root, unless the clone's baseline was saved after the refresh started.
decisions.why: FR-006 says 'its baseline replaces the clone's, its coverage paths rewritten from the worktree to the clone, unless the clone's baseline is newer'. Measuring 'newer' against the moment the refresh started puts that condition into practice and does not narrow it: any clone baseline saved after the refresh began comes from a run at the same or a later tree.

decisions.id: D8 run record and worktree cleanup
decisions.summary: The worktree is removed. The refresh's run record is copied into the clone's dev/run-log/ and committed path by path.
decisions.why: This serves item 2 / FR-002 (every full run's reason recorded in the gate's run record) and item 5 / FR-005 for the refresh's own full run. Without the copy, the refresh's record would be lost when the worktree is removed. It adds no behavior the request did not ask for.

decisions.summary: Unit tests: over-fraction landing stays incremental; refresh at >=25% and not under; never two at once; baseline copied with paths rewritten and not over a newer one.
decisions.why: These enforce FR-006 and SC-004 as FR-008 requires. They are enforcement of the request, not added scope.

decisions.summary: The no-cutoff switch becomes a make variable (NO_CUTOFF=1) that the test recipe passes to the planner's call only, instead of an INCR_NO_CUTOFF environment variable that every test in the gate inherits.
decisions.why: Item 6 / FR-006 asks that a landing's gate run what its change reaches however much; the landing still drops the cutoff, and the change only stops the switch leaking into the tests the gate runs. What the planner does on a landing is unchanged.

decisions.summary: The T03 test starts a stand-in check rather than the real cover_changed.py, so its nested coverage run no longer overwrites the gate's coverage data.
decisions.why: FR-004 (item 4) is about land.py running cover-changed beside the gate, stopping the gate when it refuses and refusing the landing. A stand-in that passes or refuses still exercises that orchestration, so FR-008's test of the behavior stays in place and only its isolation from the gate running it changes.

decisions.summary: The planner tests clear the no-cutoff variable themselves as a backstop.
decisions.why: This isolates the tests and narrows nothing: the tests keep checking the planner's behavior both with the cutoff and without it, as FR-006 and FR-008 require.

decisions.summary: The next step is one make land for T05, with the three planner tests green and nothing new failing.
decisions.why: This is a verification step under the arbiter's continue ruling. It does not alter the measurement basis the GM approved in amendment 1 or any requirement.
